newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor down on separate Billiton listing.
newsitem.headline: Gencor down on separate Billiton listing.

text.p: Shares in South African mining house Gencor Ltd fell sharply on Monday following the unbundling and separate listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange of shares in its base metals arm, Billiton Plc.
By 0755 GMT Gencor shares were down 943 cents or over 50 percent to 902 cents rand in brisk volume of 130,800 shares.
Dealers said that following the restructuring, which includes a Billiton share issue and a consolidation of Gencor shares, they had expected Gencor shares to settle at between 10.00 and 11.00 rand.

But the price had fallen further as shareholders dumped stocks on concerns about the gold price, which last month fell to 12-year lows, and to which Gencor's precious metals mining operations are exposed.
"People don't want to be exposed to gold. They rather want the base metals exposure which Billiton has," one dealer said.
Billiton, which last week listed on the London Stock Exchange, on Monday listed 1.66 billion shares and 426.70 million renounceable letters of entitlement on the JSE.
The shares opened at 16.70 rand. By 0756 GMT they had traded in a narrow 16.50-70 band, last sitting tight at the upper end of the range, in volume of 85,100 shares.
According to the Billiton prospectus, shareholders holding 100 Gencor shares on Friday will receive 75 shares in Billiton plus 25 letters of entitlement in Billiton.
At the same time a one-for-five share consolidation in Gencor meant that shareholders would receive an extra 20 Gencor shares.
Billiton last Tuesday gained instant blue chip status on the London stock market after successfully placing 375 million new shares at 220 pence -- well within the 210-240 range set earlier by Gencor.
The placing is part of the group's demerger with Gencor, which will focus on its precious metals operations while Billiton seeks to expand beyond its home base.
No longer hampered by South African exchange controls, Billiton wants to expand existing operations while also eyeing privatisation projects in countries such as Venezuela, Colombia and Brazil.
